name: typespeed
desc: Zap words flying across the screen by typing them correctly
why: A ncurses typing game in the old-school style, charming but close to the many typing trainers out there.

brief.what_it_is: Typespeed is a terminal typing game written in C that uses curses for its menu and game screens. Words fly across the screen from left to right, and the player zaps them by typing them correctly. The game is over after 10 or more missed words. It has a single-player mode with a top-10 high score list, configurable through simple 'game rules' files, and a multiplayer mode over TCP/IPv4 where words you type are sent to your opponent's screen.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says the idea is taken from ztspeed, a DOS game by Zorlim, and describes the game as testing your typing speed and getting your fingers' CPS (characters per second).
brief.how_it_works: Words scroll across the screen and speed up linearly as you type correct words, with pausing allowed in single-player. Multiplayer is a TCP/IPv4 connection, either over the internet or on a LAN, where words typed by either player are thrown into the other player's game. Single-player behaviour is set through configuration files called game rules, which control things like speed and how many missed words end the game. A random seed from an earlier game can be supplied so two players get the same word sequence.

brief.install_notes: The homepage says to use your system's package handbook for a packaged port. To build from source you need working development tools: gcc, make, and the curses headers. Pre-built packages listed are old: Fedora Core 6 rpm, Mandriva 2008 rpm, PS2 Linux rpm, Slackware tgz, and a 32-bit Windows zip built with MinGW and pdcurses. Multiplayer needs a TCP/IPv4 connection or a LAN. Upgrading from versions before 0.6.3 breaks multiplayer compatibility, and old high scores need converting with the convert tool. No Homebrew-specific notes were on the page.
brief.standout: The multiplayer mode is the distinctive part: you can attack an opponent by sending them the words you type, so accuracy and speed both matter in a head-to-head game. The configurable game rules files and the optional random seed for sharing a word sequence are also more than a plain typing trainer offers.
brief.status: quiet. The newest release on the homepage is 0.6.5, dated 2008-08-13, and the most recent news item is from the same date. Nothing on the page shows activity after 2008, so I cannot confirm it is still maintained.
brief.caveats: Last release was in 2008 and the page does not mention anything newer. Development is said to focus on GNU/Linux x86_64 with ncurses; other POSIX systems are supported in principle. The Windows port is 32-bit and lacks some functionality. Multiplayer uses a network code rewrite from 0.6.3 and there is no mention of encryption or NAT traversal. The page lists the copyright as 1999-2008 with a permissive notice, and no license name is given. The brew caveats field was empty.
